parts.latex:
Ashan's mathematics class needs to complete six tests, each worth 100 marks.

After completing the first five tests, Ashan calculated that he would need a mark of 90 in the final test in order to have a mean mark of 80 for the six tests.

What was Ashan's mean mark after completing the first five tests?

solutions.latex:
For a mean of 80 over six tests, the total of the six marks must be
$$6\times 80 = 480$$
The final mark needed is 90, so the first five tests total
$$480 - 90 = 390$$
The mean after five tests is
$$\dfrac{390}{5} = 78$$
This is option A.

parts.latex:
Consider the following dataset.

$$13 \quad 16 \quad 17 \quad 17 \quad 21 \quad 24$$

Which row of the table shows how the median and mean are affected when a score of 5 is added to the dataset?

solutions.latex:
Original dataset (6 scores): $13,\ 16,\ 17,\ 17,\ 21,\ 24$.

The median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th scores:
$$\dfrac{17+17}{2}=17$$
The mean is:
$$\dfrac{13+16+17+17+21+24}{6}=\dfrac{108}{6}=18$$
After adding 5 there are 7 scores: $5,\ 13,\ 16,\ 17,\ 17,\ 21,\ 24$.

The median is the 4th score, which is 17, so the median stays the same.

The new mean is:
$$\dfrac{108+5}{7}=\dfrac{113}{7}\approx 16.1$$
so the mean changes.

So the median stays the same and the mean changes, option D.

parts.latex:
Consider the following dataset.

$$1 \quad 5 \quad 9 \quad 10 \quad 15$$

Suppose a new value, $x$, is added to this dataset, giving the following.

$$1 \quad 5 \quad 9 \quad 10 \quad 15 \quad x$$

It is known that $x$ is greater than 15. It is also known that the difference between the means of the two datasets is equal to ten times the difference between the medians of the two datasets.

Calculate the value of $x$.

solutions.latex:
For the first dataset:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{mean} &= \dfrac{1+5+9+10+15}{5} = 8 \\ \text{median} &= 9 \end{aligned}$$
For the second dataset, since $x>15$ it is the largest value:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{mean} &= \dfrac{40+x}{6} \\ \text{median} &= \dfrac{9+10}{2} = 9.5 \end{aligned}$$
The difference in means equals ten times the difference in medians:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{40+x}{6}-8 &= 10(9.5-9) \\ \dfrac{40+x}{6}-8 &= 5 \\ \dfrac{40+x}{6} &= 13 \\ 40+x &= 78 \\ x &= 38 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = 38$$
criteria: Calculates the mean and median of the first dataset and the mean of the second dataset, or equivalent merit
Calculates mean and median of first dataset, or equivalent merit
Calculates median of first dataset, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A dataset consists of four whole numbers: $X$, $Y$, 34 and $Z$, where

\begin{itemize}
\item $X$, $Y$, 34 and $Z$ are in ascending order, and
\item $Z = X + 38$.
\end{itemize}

The median of this dataset is 26 and the mean is 28.

What is the value of $X$?

solutions.latex:
The median is the mean of the two middle values, $Y$ and 34.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{Y + 34}{2} &= 26 \\ Y &= 18 \end{aligned}$$
The mean is 28, and $Z = X + 38$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{X + 18 + 34 + Z}{4} &= 28 \\ \dfrac{X + 18 + 34 + X + 38}{4} &= 28 \\ 2X + 90 &= 112 \\ 2X &= 22 \\ X &= 11 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ X = 11$$
criteria: Equates a correct expression for the mean to 28, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Over 7 cricket matches Adam took the following number of wickets: 4, 2, 6, 4, 0, 1 and 4. In the 8th match he took 3 wickets.

Which of these statements is true when the 8th match is included?

solutions.latex:
Find the mean of the first 7 matches.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Mean} &= \dfrac{4+2+6+4+0+1+4}{7} \\ &= \dfrac{21}{7} = 3 \end{aligned}$$
The 8th score is $3$, which equals the mean, so the mean stays at $3$.

The standard deviation depends on the sum of squared deviations from the mean.
$$\begin{aligned} \sum (x-3)^2 &= 1+1+9+1+9+4+1 \\ &= 26 \end{aligned}$$
The new score $3$ has deviation $0$, so the sum stays $26$ but is now divided by $8$ instead of $7$ (population standard deviation).
$$\sqrt{\dfrac{26}{7}} \approx 1.93 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sqrt{\dfrac{26}{8}} \approx 1.80$$
So the standard deviation decreases. (The sample standard deviation gives the same conclusion: $\sqrt{\dfrac{26}{6}} \approx 2.08$ falls to $\sqrt{\dfrac{26}{7}} \approx 1.93$.)

Therefore the mean stays the same and the standard deviation decreases, which is option B.

meta.self_check: Computed mean 3 and sum of squared deviations 26 in python-free hand check; SD falls under both population and sample formulas.

parts.latex:
When an additional score is added to the data set below, the mean increases slightly, but the median remains the same.

Data Set: $1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 7, 7, 8$

Which of the following could have been the additional score?

solutions.latex:
The data set has 8 scores, so the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th scores:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{median} &= \dfrac{5 + 7}{2} \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}$$
The mean is $\dfrac{40}{8} = 5$.

With 9 scores, the median is the 5th score. For it to remain $6$, the new score must be $6$.

Adding $6$ gives a mean of $\dfrac{46}{9} \approx 5.1$, a slight increase.

Other options: adding $4$ or $5$ makes the median $5$, and adding $7$ makes the median $7$.

parts.latex: Which of the following datasets has a median of 50 and a mean of 60?

solutions.latex:
The median is the middle score (or the mean of the two middle scores) and the mean is the sum divided by the number of scores. Test each dataset.

Option A: the median is $\dfrac{60+70}{2}=65$, so A fails.

Option B: the median is $\dfrac{50+50}{2}=50$, but the sum is $320$, so the mean is $\dfrac{320}{6}\approx 53.3$. B fails.

Option C: the median is $\dfrac{45+55}{2}=50$, but the sum is $340$, so the mean is $\dfrac{340}{6}\approx 56.7$. C fails.

Option D: the median is $\dfrac{45+55}{2}=50$ and the sum is
$$40+45+45+55+85+90=360$$
so the mean is $\dfrac{360}{6}=60$.

$$\therefore\ \text{the dataset in option D has median 50 and mean 60}$$

parts.latex:
Gordon rated eleven restaurants out of 10. His ratings are listed below.

$$3,\ 3,\ 4,\ 4,\ 4,\ 5,\ 7,\ 7,\ 8,\ 9,\ 9$$

Gordon visited a new restaurant and rated it, adding the rating to the list above. The new rating did not affect the median, but did lower the mean.

Find the rating Gordon gave the new restaurant.

solutions.latex:
The current median is $5$ and the current mean is $5.72$.

For the median to stay unchanged, the new rating must be $5$.

This also lowers the mean, since $5<5.72$.
$$\therefore \text{the new rating is } 5$$
